Care-management targeting prototype

Predict next-year admission, group members into phenotypes, then choose whom to contact with limited capacity. Research prototype on CMS synthetic Medicare claims (DE-SynPUF Sample 1).

Synthetic data, assumed effects. CMS DE-SynPUF is synthetic. No clinical or epidemiological conclusion is valid from these numbers. The intervention effect (10–30% fewer admissions) is an assumption, not a measurement. Only a randomized pilot can measure it.

0.74
AUROC for next-year admission (95% CI 0.73–0.75)
8
stable phenotypes from 2008 conditions and use
345 vs 135
2009 admissions among 714 contacted members: risk-targeted vs random

1. Whom to contact

2. Do the assumptions change the answer?

3. Phenotypes

4. Are the risk numbers honest? (calibration)

5. Subgroup check

6. What drives the risk score

7. Measuring a program effect (simulated)

The program and its true effect are simulated so the right answer is known. Sicker members were made more likely to enroll. A naive enrolled-vs-not comparison is biased; propensity-score methods recover the effect only when the confounders are measured.

8. Forecasting monthly admissions

Only 22 usable months: too short for seasonal models. Simple methods were compared in a rolling backtest; interval coverage is reported with its uncertainty.
